title: Perpetua and Felicity (203)
hookLine: a young noblewoman and her enslaved companion, whose own prison diary survives

cards: The darkness scared her. She had never known a place like it. The heat of the crowd, the soldiers shoving, and worst of all, worry for her baby.

A young mother wrote that, in a prison in North Africa. Her name was Vibia Perpetua: well born, educated, married, nursing an infant son. Arrested with her was Felicity, an enslaved woman, heavily pregnant.
They were catechumens, still preparing for baptism. And because Perpetua kept a record, her own words survive.

teach.b: The text is called the Passion of Perpetua and Felicity. First, her own hand. The narrator says that from here on, Perpetua tells the story herself, as she left it written with her own hand.
A prisoner's notes, from the inside.
Second, the baby. Deacons pay the guards so the prisoners can move to a better part of the jail for a few hours, and Perpetua nurses her son.
When she's allowed to keep him with her, she writes that the prison suddenly felt like a palace. Her father comes again and again, begging her to give in for his sake and the child's.
She grieves for him, and she doesn't give in. Third, Felicity. Pregnant women weren't put to death, and she's afraid she'll be held back while her friends die without her.
Her companions pray with her, and she goes into labor. A guard sneers: if you cry out like this now, what will you do in front of the beasts? She answers: now I'm the one who suffers.
Then another will be in me, who will suffer for me, because I'll be suffering for him.
She gives birth to a daughter, and a Christian woman raises the girl as her own. Fourth, the arena.

teach.h: SHE LIFTS HER TO HER FEET.
teach.b: The text says Perpetua, thrown down, gets up, sees Felicity on the ground, and lifts her to her feet. The two stand together.
Before they die, they give each other the kiss of peace. A noblewoman and an enslaved woman. At Mass, the first Eucharistic Prayer still names them both.

how: Catholics keep Saints Perpetua and Felicity as a memorial in the Church's calendar, and both are named among the martyrs in the Roman Canon, the first Eucharistic Prayer of the Mass.

games.q: you're Felicity, in labor in the prison. a guard sneers: if you cry out now, what will you do in front of the beasts? what do you say?
o: now I suffer; then another will suffer in me.
games.why: Felicity says that now she is the one suffering, but then another will be in her who will suffer for her, because she will be suffering for him.

practice: Bring to mind a young mother you know, a friend, a sister, a neighbor, or someone you saw on the bus with a stroller and a tired face. Think of the night feeds, the worry, the not knowing, and hold her there a while.
If you pray, ask God to give her rest and help; if you don't, simply wish her strength.
